title: Compound Interest Calculator - Daily & Regular Deposits
description: Calculate compound interest with daily, monthly, quarterly, or annual compounding and optional regular deposits with visual growth charts. Free tool.
quickAnswer: Compound interest is calculated using the formula A = P(1 + r/n)^(nt), where P is principal, r is annual interest rate (decimal), n is compounding frequency per year, and t is time in years. When making regular monthly deposits PMT, future value also compounds via the annuity formula: PMT × [((1 + r/n)^(nt) - 1) / (r/n)]. All calculations and growth charts run in your browser.

formula.title: Compound Interest Formula
formula.explanation: Without contributions, future value A grows from principal P at annual rate r, compounded n times per year for t years, earning interest on accumulated interest.

commonMistakes.title: Comparing APR to APY Directly
commonMistakes.description: A bank advertising 5.00% APR with daily compounding actually pays 5.13% APY. Always compare APY against APY for true apples-to-apples evaluation.

commonMistakes.title: Delaying Contributions
commonMistakes.description: Thanks to geometric exponential growth, depositing early in your twenties compounds far more wealth than depositing twice as much later in your forties.

commonMistakes.title: Ignoring Inflation & Taxes
commonMistakes.description: High nominal interest rates must be adjusted for inflation and annual tax obligations on interest income to gauge real purchasing power growth.

howto.name: How to Calculate Compound Interest Growth
howto.description: Step-by-step instructions for modeling compounding frequencies, periodic deposits, and annual percentage yields (APY).

steps.name: Enter Starting Principal
steps.text: Input your initial lump sum investment or savings balance (can be $0 if starting purely with regular deposits).

steps.name: Enter Annual Interest Rate
steps.text: Input the nominal annual percentage rate (APR) earned by your high-yield savings account, CD, or investment.

steps.name: Select Compounding Frequency

steps.name: Set Investment Time Horizon
steps.text: Specify how many years you plan to allow your money to compound untouched.

steps.name: Add Optional Monthly Contributions
steps.text: Optionally enter recurring monthly deposits to project exponential dollar-cost growth.

steps.name: Review Visual Growth Chart & Balances
steps.text: Inspect your final future value, total interest earned, effective APY, and interactive SVG growth trajectory chart.

faqs.q: What is the difference between simple interest and compound interest?
faqs.a: Simple interest calculates interest solely on the original principal amount. Compound interest calculates interest on both the initial principal and the accumulated interest from prior periods, accelerating growth exponentially over time.

faqs.q: What is the mathematical compound interest formula?
faqs.a: Without periodic contributions, the formula is: A = P × (1 + r/n)^(n×t), where P is the principal, r is the annual nominal interest rate in decimal form, n is the number of compounding periods per year, and t is the time horizon in years.

faqs.q: What is the difference between APR and APY?
faqs.a: APR (Annual Percentage Rate) is the stated nominal interest rate without accounting for intraday or intramonth compounding. APY (Annual Percentage Yield) reflects the true effective annual rate including the compounding effect: APY = (1 + r/n)^n - 1.

faqs.q: How often should interest compound for maximum growth?
faqs.a: More frequent compounding produces higher effective returns. Daily compounding (365 times per year) yields slightly higher total interest than monthly (12 times) or annual (1 time) compounding for the exact same nominal interest rate.

faqs.q: Are any investment or personal balance numbers stored?
faqs.a: No. All compound interest calculations and SVG charts render purely in memory within your web browser. No private financial balances leave your device.
